scores.evidence: The rules-diagram flowchart TD stays readable at 390 px. Its Japanese labels are legible and the arrows are clear (pages/mobile-jp-09.png). The example-code and rules-files code blocks fit without wrapping (pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/mobile-jp-17.png). The mode list (modes-table) and the rewind list (rewind-table) are bullet lists rather than wide tables, so nothing sticks out sideways (overflowX false).

textOnlyScreens is empty on both desktop and mobile. Every screen has a heading, a check, a code block, the diagram or steps. Paragraphs are short and a quiz follows every concept section, so there are no walls of text in pages/mobile-jp-01.png to pages/mobile-jp-29.png.

The lesson is all Japanese with no stray English UI. Contrast is good and controls clear the top and bottom bars. Inline code chips stay whole (for example the --dangerously-skip-permissions chip in pages/mobile-jp-06.png and pages/mobile-jp-22.png). Minor points: desktop charsPerLine has a median of 41 and a max of 54, against a target of 30–40. The prompt blocks show raw backticks, and one file name splits across lines (pages/mobile-jp-21.png).

niceToHave: rewind-prompt / rules-prompt: the prompt text shows literal backticks (`git push`, `.claude/settings.json`, `rewind-practice.md`). On mobile, `rewind-copy.md` breaks into 'rewind-' / 'copy.md' (pages/mobile-jp-20.png, pages/mobile-jp-21.png). Consider 「」 quotes instead of backticks in the prompt text, so learners read the file names as names.
sort-task: on mobile, '2-1の一覧' breaks between '2-' and '1' (pages/mobile-jp-15.png). Rephrase as '前の一覧（2-1）' or put '2-1' later in the sentence.
reader: desktop charsPerLine has a median of 41 and a max of 54, against a target of 30–40. The 680 px measure at 18.7 px is slightly wide for Japanese body text.

reader: the mobile full-length PNG stops at 16000 px (truncated), and the end banner says this is the course's last lesson because drafts are not in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-29.png, pages/desktop-jp-20.png).
reader: 14 failed /api/ requests (500 on user/progress, events, notifications) are environment noise and are not counted as console errors.
summary: There are no hard failures (overflowX, console, mermaid, unknown-block and broken-image counts are all 0) and no personal data on any screen. The flowchart, code blocks and quizzes are all readable at 390 px, and every screen has a structural element. Only polish remains: the raw backticks in the two prompt blocks, the broken '2-1' on mobile, and the reader's slightly wide desktop line length.
